title: An apostle is told to prepare for a mission abroad
setting: David W. Patten, a member of the Twelve, was living in Far West, Missouri, by 1837. In April 1838, he reported he could not support several apostles who had turned against Joseph Smith. On 11 April 1838, Joseph dictated this revelation for Patten at Far West. A July 1838 revelation later set the Twelve’s mission abroad for 1839. Patten was killed in October 1838, before that mission began.
summary: The revelation tells David W. Patten to settle his business as soon as he can. He is to dispose of his merchandise. This will free him to go on a mission the next spring. He will go with others, twelve including himself, to testify to all the world. The revelation then says some among them deny the Lord’s name. Others will be planted in their place and receive their “bishopric”.

contextNote.title: Offices pass to those who stay faithful
contextNote.text: Several apostles had turned against Joseph Smith by spring 1838. Verse 1 plans a mission of “twelve including himself,” assuming a full quorum. Verse 2 explains how that will happen if some fall away. Those who “deny my name” will be replaced by others planted in their stead. Here “bishopric” means an office or charge, as in the King James wording of Acts 1:20. In this passage, the calling continues even when particular holders leave it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 111–114 includes this short revelation to David W. Patten. Why might verse 1 ask Patten to settle his business before serving, and what does verse 2 promise about the quorum?
reviewNote: Read both verses. Official heading gives Far West, 11 April 1838, to David W. Patten. JSP introduction and annotation read: Patten’s merchandise and debts, his doubts at the April 1838 conference about McLellin, Luke and Lyman Johnson, Boynton, and William Smith, and the 8 July 1838 revelation setting the 1839 mission. Patten’s death at Crooked River in October 1838 is general knowledge, not from the pages read. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
